passage.text: Hi, Nam! I'm in my hometown in Canada for a week.
passage.reading: ˈhaɪ, ˈnɑːm! aɪm ɪn maɪ ˈhoʊmtaʊn ɪn ˈkænədə fər ə ˈwiːk.

passage.text: It's a small town, and there's only one main street.
passage.reading: ɪts ə ˈsmɔːl ˈtaʊn, ənd ðɛrz ˈoʊnli ˈwʌn ˈmeɪn ˈstriːt.

passage.text: It's fall now, and the maple trees are red and orange.
passage.reading: ɪts ˈfɔːl ˈnaʊ, ənd ðə ˈmeɪpəl ˈtriːz ər ˈrɛd ənd ˈɔːrɪndʒ.

passage.text: This morning, I had coffee with my mom at a cozy café on the main street.
passage.reading: ðɪs ˈmɔːrnɪŋ, aɪ ˈhæd ˈkɔːfi wɪð maɪ ˈmɑːm ət ə ˈkoʊzi kæˈfeɪ ɑːn ðə ˈmeɪn ˈstriːt.

passage.text: It's warm and quiet, and they have the best cookies in town.
passage.reading: ɪts ˈwɔːrm ənd ˈkwaɪət, ənd ðeɪ ˈhæv ðə ˈbɛst ˈkʊkiz ɪn ˈtaʊn.

passage.text: Tonight, my little brother has a hockey game.
passage.reading: təˈnaɪt, maɪ ˈlɪtəl ˈbrʌðər ˈhæz ə ˈhɑːki ˈɡeɪm.

passage.text: Hockey is the most popular sport here, so a lot of people are going to watch.
passage.reading: ˈhɑːki ɪz ðə ˈmoʊst ˈpɑːpjələr ˈspɔːrt ˈhɪr, soʊ ə ˈlɑːt əv ˈpiːpəl ər ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈwɑːtʃ.

passage.text: I love my hometown, but there's no night market and no street food!
passage.reading: aɪ ˈlʌv maɪ ˈhoʊmtaʊn, bʌt ðɛrz ˈnoʊ ˈnaɪt ˌmɑːrkɪt ənd ˈnoʊ ˈstriːt ˈfuːd!

passage.text: Please eat some pad Thai for me!
passage.reading: ˈpliːz ˈiːt sʌm ˈpɑːd ˈtaɪ fər miː!
